metadata.title: Infrastructure reliability incident investigation
metadata.artifact_scope_note: Evidence is aggregated query output (not raw log lines or metric samples); it contains no chat/communication records.

incident_description: Reliability incident investigation of a production environment. Evidence consists of Elasticsearch aggregation results over application and proxy logs, Kubernetes, cloud-provider and host system events, Prometheus Alertmanager alerts, change-management / CI-CD audit records and metric anomaly detection. No root cause, impact or trigger is stated; these must be established from the supplied artifacts. Environment context: Organization: Lumix Goods (online retail); Platform: Google Cloud southamerica-east1 (zones southamerica-east1-a/southamerica-east1-b/southamerica-east1-c); network range 10.34.0.0/16; Kubernetes cluster lumix-prod-southa (GKE); Database: mysql server inventory-db-01 reachable from the application network only through firewall rule allow-inventory-to-db; infrastructure is managed with Terraform applied from CI; Change management: production changes carry RFC- identifiers.
investigation_questions: What change, deployment or automation run triggered the incident? Provide its change identifier.
Who (account or automation identity) executed the change that caused the incident?
What is the IP address of the database host that became unreachable?
Which network control object was modified?
During what hour did the first signs of the failure appear? Provide the earliest date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC format.

What is the root cause category of the incident: configuration change, software defect, hardware failure, cloud provider failure, capacity exhaustion, automation error, certificate expiry, or third-party dependency failure?
Which of the three CIA components is primarily affected: availability, integrity, or confidentiality?
According to the error volume statistics, what single service emitted the most errors? Is it the root cause or a downstream symptom?
Which change happened shortly before the incident began but did not cause it? Provide its identifier.
What change brought the service back to normal? Give its identifier.
